Note::TexAccessor::strip_size¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_size() const

Remove Explicit Delimiter-Size Commands¶

strip_size() removes the twelve delimiter-sizing control words \big, \Big, \bigg, \Bigg, and their l/r forms. The delimiter characters that follow remain, so \Bigl( x \Bigr) becomes ( x ) rather than losing the parentheses or their contents.

Matching is by complete control-word name. Escaped commands and longer names such as \BiglExtra are untouched. The method does not remove \left or \right, alter delimiter characters, or validate pairing; it addresses only explicit big-family size annotations.

ASCII whitespace is collapsed and cells are trimmed after rewriting. The operation allocates a shape-preserving Text Note and leaves its receiver unchanged. Undefined input propagates and non-Text input rejects. The scanner is linear and performs no regular-expression replacement passes.

Example 1: Every Match Leaves Its Delimiter¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\Bigl( x \Bigr) + \bigg[y\bigg])",
    R"(\\Bigl literal \BiglExtra keep)", "plain"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_size() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["( x ) + [y]", "\\\\Bigl literal \\BiglExtra keep", "plain"]

Example 2: Delimiter Families And Non-Targets¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\bigl\{a\bigr\})", R"(\Bigg|x\Bigg|)",
                             R"(\left(y\right))", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_size();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_size()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["\\{a\\}", "|x|"], 
  ["\\left(y\\right)", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

Escaped braces and vertical bars are delimiter tokens and remain. Automatic \left/\right sizing is a separate construct and is deliberately untouched.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_size().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_size();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip size Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip size Int64: rejected
